definitions.explanation: A group sharing the same interests or goals, especially in literary/artistic circles
Modern usage: amateur self-published works, especially manga, games, and music

⟦{文学|ぶんがく}→文学：01505_bungaku⟧{同人|どうじん}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{活動|かつどう}→活動：00201_katsudou⟧⟦していた→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I was active as part of a literary coterie.

notes:
Originally refers to people who share the same interests or ideals, particularly in literary and artistic circles. In modern Japanese, overwhelmingly associated with fan-produced and self-published creative works, especially manga.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{同人誌|どうじんし}→同人誌：07326_doujinshi⟧: doujinshi — a self-published magazine or book
- {同人|どうじん}⟦サークル→サークル：10933_saakuru⟧: doujin circle — a group that creates and sells amateur works
- {同人|どうじん}⟦イベント→イベント：09594_ibento⟧: doujin event
- {同人|どうじん}{即売会|そくばいかい}: doujin sales event (like Comiket)
- {同人|どうじん}⟦ゲーム→ゲーム：03842_geemu⟧: doujin game — amateur-produced video game
- {同人|どうじん}⟦{活動|かつどう}→活動：00201_katsudou⟧: doujin activities

CULTURAL NOTE:
The largest {同人|どうじん}{即売会|そくばいかい} is コミケ (Comiket, Comic Market), held twice a year in Tokyo. {同人|どうじん} culture is a major part of Japanese otaku culture, with thousands of amateur creators producing original and fan-based works.
